summary: Round 4. THE DELTA CLAIM IS VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, not taken from the packet: `git diff f24e3ac6f64ff93af91921729a70a71f6d38351e $(git write-tree)` -- the round-3 verdict's own recorded staged_tree against the tree I am judging -- is exactly `baselines/review.txt | 1 +`, one added line, zero deletions. No source file, no test, no javadoc moved; Invariants.java and AckOrderTest.java are byte-identical to the bytes I passed at 55efbfba63a6. No build run this round and none is meaningful: the delta is one prose line in a text file, so there is no mutation to measure and I state that rather than implying a suite ran. Cost lens: the added line is prose in baselines/; it issues no get/put/list/stat and changes no request rate. THE ARGUMENT ITSELF, CHECKED CLAIM BY CLAIM AGAINST THE VERDICT FILES RATHER THAN READ FOR PLAUSIBILITY -- every factual assertion holds. Round 1's two measurements: `d355d7f8d508.reviewer` records a two-chain trace where the successor acks its sequence 2 having confirmed nothing of its own returning ZERO violations, and a strictly serial trace based at 1000 returning FOUR; `d355d7f8d508.test-reviewer` records CommitLog.java:192 advancing nextSequence past the CONTINUE, so the production numbering is the worse case. Round 2's two: `3e8198a5ef96.test-reviewer` measured `while (seen.contains(w))` -> `if` passing all 10 AckOrderTest tests, and the watermark keyed on a constant passing all 10 -- the entry's 'depth 3 added only to the violation side' and 'keyed per-epoch but no trace interleaved epochs' are both exactly what was filed. Round 3: reviewer pass/0 findings, test-reviewer pass/1 finding whose own note says 'the arm is round-1 code that already carries a verdict' -- so 'found nothing new in the delta and both reviewers PASSED' is accurate, not a rounding of a changes-requested into a pass. 'Four tests were added' is right: 10 tests at round 2, 14 at round 3. NO SEAM EXISTS AND I LOOKED FOR ONE, since M0.79's entry three lines above is a case where a seam was denied and review found it. Predicate-and-its-tests is not splittable in the direction proposed: non-negotiable 3 forbids landing production before the test that failed against it, so 'the predicate' as a commit is unbuildable, and 'the cases that pin it' as a follow-up would land a checker with the surviving mutations rounds 1-2 measured -- against a row whose own text warns that a test written here can pass while constraining nothing. Splitting at the ROUND-2 boundary was also unavailable: the round-2 test-reviewer verdict was changes-requested on two majors, so nothing could land there. The remaining candidate, the backlog-notes.md M4.22 and M4.13 notes, are prose about the code in this same diff and separating them would leave a note pointing at a checker no commit carries. The exceedance is warranted: rounds 1 and 2 each found real, measured defects in the code the previous round shipped, round 3 verified, and round 4 exists only because staging the argument moves the hash -- which review_rounds.py's own docstring states is unavoidable. One minor filed on what the entry does NOT say.

findings.title: The entry accounts for three rounds; the counter that fires the cap says four, and this entry is the only `rounds:` line in the file that does not name the round it created
findings.detail: The entry's only count is 'that is the honest reason there were three', and it describes rounds 1, 2 and 3. `review_rounds.py` counts distinct reviewed hashes for the task and will return 4 the moment this round's verdicts land -- its docstring says so explicitly: 'staging an argument DOES move the hash and DOES cost a round'. The three sibling entries do name their in-flight round and what it held: M0.79 'Splitting at round 4 costs four fresh rounds', M4.10c 'ROUND 6 IS PROSE ONLY', M4.10d 'Round 6 reviews that correction and a note moved to M4.10f, no production change'. This one stops at three.
findings.failure_scenario: The next author past the cap greps baselines/review.txt for what an argued exception has cost before, which is the only place in the tree that records it, and reads three where `python3 scripts/review_rounds.py --for-task M4.11` returns 4. This project already uses those counts as evidence in load-bearing places -- check-reviewed.sh's own comment argues the cap from '8 of 12 tasks in one session' and 'AT LEAST NINE commits in M4', and M0.47's row calls 8 the repository record -- so an entry that undercounts its own rounds by one feeds a low number into the next argument about whether the escape is being overused. It is the same shape as the failure the M4.10d entry records against itself, one copy of a count corrected and another left saying something else, at a much smaller scale.
findings.fix: One clause, e.g. 'ROUND 4 IS THIS ENTRY: staging the argument moves the hash, which review_rounds.py counts as a round, so the recorded total is four and no code changed in it.' NOT worth a fifth round on its own -- the commit body carries it, or the clause goes in whenever this entry is next touched.
